reply.subject: RM_Shirrel

observed.facings.png: Three grounded facings side by side at one scale. South: a heavy, deep-chested grey-and-ochre quadruped with tall tufted lynx-like ears, a narrow feline face and white chevron bands on its shoulders. Its bushy banded tail sweeps out to the left. East: a long low profile with a folded membrane lying along the flank in slate and cream bands, whiskered snout, big hooked claws, long brush tail. North: the rear, with haunches, a tail hanging down the middle, the ears' backs and no face. East is visibly shorter than south because it is a low profile pose.
observed.south.png: The grounded front view at full resolution. The face looks at the camera, the chest is deep, the shoulders carry banded folds and the claws are prominent. Painterly, clean alpha.
observed.east.png: The grounded side profile. The membrane is folded along the flank in slate and fog-white bands. Deep chest, strong curved claws, brush tail. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: The grounded rear view: back, haunches, banded flank folds and a hanging tail with a cream tip. Ear backs show; there is no face or eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: The grounded south sprite next to the vanilla human at max zoom. It is roughly a large cat to small dog in size, about two thirds of the human's body height. At 32 px per cell it is a small grey shape with a pale tail, readable as an animal next to the rat and human.
observed.flight_1.png: East flight frame 1, a side view in a glide. The body is stretched flat, all four limbs reach out to the wrists and ankles, and a membrane runs along the whole flank with slate and fog-white wavy bands. Hooked claws show on all four feet, the lynx-eared head faces right and the bushy tail trails left. The torso looks slimmer and more squirrel-like than the grounded body. Clean alpha.
observed.flight_2.png: Looks identical to frame 1 at normal viewing. Code shows about 700 px differ inside the membrane and the silhouette bbox is unchanged.
observed.flight_3.png: Looks identical to frame 1. About 1050 px differ inside the membrane; silhouette unchanged.
observed.flight_4.png: Matches frame 2, the ping-pong frame, as the card says it should.
observed.flight_5.png: North flight frame 1, the rear seen from behind and above. The spread membrane forms a broad rectangle with pale bands, the four limbs end in claws at the corners, a dark spine stripe runs up the middle, ear tips show at the far top edge and a big cream-tipped tail hangs toward the camera. No face or eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.flight_6.png: Looks identical to frame 5. About 311 px differ; silhouette unchanged.
observed.flight_7.png: Looks identical to frame 5. About 492 px differ; silhouette unchanged.
observed.flight_9.png: South flight frame 1, the front. The lynx face with tufted ears looks at the camera, there is a pale chest ruff, and the membrane spreads to both sides with slate and fog-white bands. Clawed hands and feet sit at the membrane corners. The tail rises behind the head (it trails away from the camera). Clean alpha.
observed.flight_10.png: Almost identical to frame 9. About 1780 px differ in the membrane bands; silhouette unchanged.
observed.flight_11.png: Almost identical to frame 9. About 2660 px differ; silhouette unchanged.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: flight_9-12 show the face, eyes and chest ruff toward the camera, with the membrane spread to both sides.

NORTH_REAR.seen: flight_5-8 show the back, spine stripe, ear backs and the tail toward the camera. No face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: The north flight frames show the dorsal side of a spread glider, but the camera reads as behind and above: the tail comes toward the viewer and the ears sit at the far edge. East is a true profile and south is a front-under view. North is close to overhead and is noted as polish.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Flight silhouettes span about 220-226 px wide in all three directions. The flagged 19% height spread is on the owner-kept grounded sprites and comes from pose (the low east profile versus the upright south), not from a scale jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same palette, lynx ears, banded membrane, claws and brush tail appear in every direction. The membrane turns with the body: a flank strip on east, a spread sheet on north and south.

SIGNATURE.seen: A full body-length gliding membrane from wrist to ankle is spread and clearly legible in every flight direction.

ALIEN.seen: The east flight frames read close to a flying squirrel. The banded storm-grey membrane, lynx ears/face and big claws hold up the departures, and the grounded art is owner-kept.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) Membrane from wrist to ankle, banded slate and fog-white: present in all frames. 2) Cat-sized and heavy-bodied with a deep keel: on scale.png the size reads cat-sized, and south flight shows a broad chest, but east flight's torso is slimmer than the grounded body (polish). 3) Strong prominent claws: present on all four feet in every direction.

STYLE.seen: Painterly fur and dark outline matching the grounded art. Not cartoon or 3D.

OURS.seen: The pipeline provenance shows the flight frames were built from the subject's own masters. No vanilla or donor look.

ALPHA.seen: All frames are clean cut-outs with no ground patch or shadow.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The body plate is locked: the silhouette bbox is identical across frames and only the membrane changes. Frame 4 equals frame 2 (ping-pong). The frames are drawn at drawSize 1.2, matching the grounded body width. The billow is barely visible, though.

SCALE.seen: On scale.png it is cat-to-small-dog size beside the human, which fits 'cat-sized'.

LEGIBLE.seen: The spread membrane makes a broad pale-banded shape that will read at 32 px. The grounded sprite is legible on the 32 px panel.

WINGS_FOLDED.seen: The grounded sprites (owner-kept) show the membrane folded along the flanks, symmetric on north.

findings.seen: Consecutive frames look identical at normal and max zoom. The silhouette bbox is unchanged and only 300-2700 interior px differ, so the promised 1.0/1.15/1.30 vertical billow of the membrane edge cannot be seen and the glide will look like a static sprite.
findings.quote: the body stays locked and only the membrane edge billows
findings.fix: The membrane's trailing edge visibly lifts and sags across frames 1-3, a few pixels of silhouette change at 128 px/cell, while the head, torso and limbs stay pixel-identical.

findings.seen: In the side glide the torso is slim and flat like a flying squirrel's. The deep-keeled chest and heavy body of the grounded east sprite are not obvious.
findings.quote: cat-sized and heavy-bodied with a deep-keeled chest, not a slim small squirrel
findings.fix: The east glide shows a thick, deep-keeled chest bulging below the membrane line, matching the heavy grounded body.

findings.seen: The north glide shows a flat dorsal plan of the spread membrane, close to overhead. The ears only peek over the far edge, so the 35-degree camera tilt reads weakly.
findings.quote: None of them is an overhead view.
findings.fix: The north glide shows the rear from behind and slightly above: back, haunches and tail toward the camera, with the membrane in foreshortened perspective and the head partly visible behind the shoulders.

reply.subject: RM_Shirrel
reply.image_seen: Image 1 shows three grounded facings; images 2–4 show their individual front, side and rear views; image 5 compares size with a human and rat; image 6 shows twelve spread-membrane flight frames in three directional rows.

concerns.evidence: The east row shows a fuller downward bow through the lower membrane and fog-white band in flight_3 than flight_1, with intermediate shapes in flight_2 and flight_4. The head, paws and tail remain anchored. The movement is subtle, consistent with billowing during a glide; unchanged bounding-box extremes do not establish an unchanged membrane contour.

Flight_1–4 retain a thick rounded hindquarter and a substantial golden chest descending beneath the neck toward the lower forelimb. The extended membrane covers much of the flank, but the visible forequarters and chest remain deep rather than showing a thin squirrel torso.

Flight_5–8 show a raised central back obscuring most of the head, with the ears projecting beyond it. The fore-to-hind membrane span is strongly foreshortened relative to its lateral spread, and the tail descends from the near rump. These depth and occlusion cues support an oblique rear view rather than an overhead plan.
